rv.q: Lavin’s exceptional performance as the brittle matriarch of this messed-up clan removes any doubt that she made the right choice.
And they’re a family that you will really, really want to spend time with. Honestly.
Lavin is an absolute wonder to behold as Rita Lyons.
When Rita finally tells her kids what’s what, you want to stand up and cheer — for the character, and for the brilliant actress bringing her to life.

One of the reasons we expect so much out of Broadway shows is that they cost so much to see. Nicky Silver's "The Lyons," which transferred to Broadway this week, is a clever little dysfunctional-family comedy that contains at least twice its fair share of laughs. Though it's more than a bit of a mes...
Silver has given her some of the best and bitchiest lines, but Lavin’s special gift is finding nuance not even in the script.

The hospital scenes crackle with an amphetamine-induced dexterity, pinballing from disorder (Curtis' mental instability) to disappointment (Lisa's failed marriage) to disease (Ben's cancer of the...whatever) to disparagement (Rita calling her grandson possibly ''slightly retarded'').

In a Broadway season full of transfers from Off-Broadway, Nicky Silver's 'The Lyons' comes charging onto the Great White Way with a savage roar that is simultaneously a scream of pain and a shout of dark laughter.
And there’s enough funny lashing to leave an audience happily smarting.
As a dysfunctional family drama, "The Lyons" is hardly as penetrating as "Clybourne Park" or "Other Desert Cities."
But that half, taking the notion of family dysfunction to the outer limits of humor, is darkly entertaining theater.
